$comment: Queries that legitimately touch a tenant-scoped table WITHOUT a tenant_id predicate.
PLAN.md 8.2 requires every entry to carry a written reason. Nothing goes in here to
silence a warning -- an entry is a claim that cross-tenant exposure is impossible by
some other means, and that claim has to hold on its own.
Tables with no tenant_id column at all are exempt automatically (the audit derives the
tenant-scoped set from prisma/schema.prisma) and need no entry here. `tenants` is the
only such table: its primary key IS the tenant id.

allow.reason: Lookup by primary key using a user id taken from the already-verified session JWT. The id is not attacker-supplied: it was signed by this server at login. Adding a tenant filter would change behaviour, and the tenant in the session came from the same signed payload.

Login is deliberately cross-tenant: the caller has no session yet, so there is no tenant to scope to. The tenant is DERIVED from the row the password selects and then signed into the session. The lookup is a findMany returning every row with that contact, oldest first, capped at MAX_CANDIDATES + 1 (11) rows, of which at most 10 are bcrypt-compared. Each password match then passes the account/firm-health gate (inactive account, disabled or suspended firm -> 403). No password match is a 401; if every match is gated, the oldest match's 403 is returned. If exactly one live company matches, that row is signed in. If MORE THAN ONE eligible account matches (same phone and same password in several live firms) the route no longer picks one: it logs [AMBIGUOUS-DUPLICATE-PHONE] and returns 200 {chooseCompany: [{tenantId, companyName}]} with NO cookie. Only tenants whose own row just matched this password and passed the health gate are listed, so the names reveal nothing to a caller without valid credentials. A second POST carrying tenantId (shape-checked, else 400) re-runs this same lookup and full password verification from scratch -- nothing from the first call is trusted -- and tenantId only selects among that request's matched rows: a tenantId not among them gets the same flat 401 as a wrong password, and a matched but gated row gets its own 403. So a session is only ever issued for a row whose phone and password the caller has just proven. Beyond chooseCompany, no row data is returned -- the response is {ok:true} plus a cookie, or a 400/401/403 -- so a non-matching row leaks nothing. Pattern is pinned to the projection containing "password", which only this query selects, so it cannot cover an unrelated unfiltered users query.

allow.source: src/lib/auth.ts requireUser(), reached from src/app/api/auth/me/route.ts and every route that calls requireUser()
allow.reason: Primary-key lookup of the session's own user id (signed JWT) that reads credentials_version, alongside profile, status and role, to compare against the token's cv. /api/auth/me no longer issues its own query -- it calls requireUser() -- and that statement is also matched by auth-requireuser-pk, which is listed first and so is the entry the audit reports. This entry is therefore currently redundant; it stays pinned to the credentials_version projection so it covers nothing auth-requireuser-pk does not. The value is compared, never returned.

Counts rows whose viewer_user_id is the session's own user id, which is itself tenant-bound. Returns only a boolean (count > 0) to the caller, never row content. Matches the pre-existing query, which was also not tenant-scoped.

Writes by primary key to a row the request already resolved: login's cleartext-to-bcrypt rehash targets the row whose password just matched; forgot-password writes the reset token to the row found by a tenant_id-scoped contact lookup; reset-password writes the new hash and bumps credentials_version on the row found by a tenant_id-scoped token lookup. The id is server-derived in every case, never taken from the request body.

allow.source: Prisma relation loading for `include: { <parent>: { select: { name: true } } }` in src/lib/auth.ts and the Batch 2 master routes
allow.reason: How Prisma resolves a to-one relation: a second statement fetching the related rows by PRIMARY KEY, using FK values already present on parent rows that were themselves selected under a tenant_id filter. No request input reaches these ids at read time. Cross-tenant FK values are prevented at WRITE time, not merely measured as absent: every route that takes one of these ids from a request body looks it up in the caller's own tenant through firstForeignTenantRef (src/lib/tenant-fk.ts) and refuses the write with a 400 on a miss, and the routes that write them without a body id (the location and product CSV imports, the bulk company import) derive the id from a tenant_id-scoped lookup. The database still does not ENFORCE it -- every FK references a bare primary key, not (tenant_id, id) -- so a write path added without the guard would reopen the hole with nothing failing; composite FKs including tenant_id are the pending structural fix recorded in PLAN.md 8.2. Tables are enumerated rather than matched by shape on purpose: a plain findMany({ where: { id: { in: ... } } }) emits identical SQL, so a blanket rule would silently swallow a genuinely missing filter.

allow.source: src/app/api/masters/users/route.ts — include: { users: { select: { id, name } } }, the manager embed
allow.reason: Prisma loading the users self-relation (manager_user_id -> users.id) for the aliased `manager` embed. Same class as prisma-to-one-relation-fetch, kept as its own entry because `users` is queried in many other places and a loose pattern here would be dangerous: the pattern is pinned to the exact id+name projection this embed emits. The manager ids come from rows already selected under tenant_id, and manager_user_id is written only by /api/masters/users POST, /api/masters/users/[id] PUT and its PATCH reactivate action, all of which validate it in the caller's tenant through firstForeignTenantRef (userFkChecks) before the write. The DB FK references users.id alone, so this rests on that write-side guard until the composite FKs in PLAN.md 8.2 land. Note the other id-IN query on users (the scope=manage visibility filter in the same route) DOES carry tenant_id and so is never flagged.

allow.source: src/app/api/weekly-plans/review/route.ts — the users!user_id(id, name, contact) embed
allow.reason: Prisma loading the plan owner for the review list. Pinned to the exact id+name+contact projection this embed emits, so it cannot match an unrelated unfiltered users query. The owner ids come from weekly_plans rows already selected under tenant_id, and weekly_plans.user_id is never taken from a request body: it is the session's own user id when the plan is created. The FK references users.id alone, so the guarantee is that server-side derivation, not the database; composite FKs are pending (PLAN.md 8.2). Same class as prisma-to-one-relation-fetch and prisma-manager-self-relation-fetch, listed separately only because the projection differs.

allow.source: Prisma relation loading for include: { weekly_plan_items: … } and similar to-many embeds
allow.reason: The to-MANY counterpart of prisma-to-one-relation-fetch, and a genuinely different SQL shape: children are fetched by their PARENT FOREIGN KEY rather than by their own primary key. The parent ids come from a query already filtered by tenant_id. A child's parent id is never taken from a request body: order_items get the id of the order the same transaction just created, and weekly_plan_items / weekly_plan_audit_logs get a plan id the route has just created or looked up under tenant_id, and are written with the caller's tenant_id. The FK references the parent's bare id, so the database alone would accept a child in another tenant; the guarantee is that server-side derivation until the composite FKs in PLAN.md 8.2 land. Tables and FK columns are both enumerated rather than matched by shape, for the same reason as the to-one rule: an ordinary findMany filtered on a FK column emits identical SQL and must keep being flagged. These child tables carry their own tenant_id, so a future explicit query on them is still expected to filter it.
